clue.text: Much less room sadly for supplementary course of study

indicators.note: things going sadly have gone wrong, so the letters before it are disordered

parts.note: the fodder, twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A cramped classroom is lamented by someone signing up for extra lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Summer school is an extra programme of classes held during the holiday, supplementing normal teaching.

clue.text: Work out near avenue in middle of July

indicators.note: in means the first pieces go inside the central letters
middle asks for the central letters of the month's name

explanation.surface: Someone does exercise near an avenue in midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' suggests the gym, but it is the definition: solve.
explanation.definitionFit: To unravel a mystery is to work it out, untangling the threads until it is clear.

clue.text: Moving some kit around globe in vehicles

indicators.note: moving the letters about puts them in a new order
around means the rearranged letters surround the next piece

explanation.surface: Travellers take equipment around the world in their vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorbikes are two-wheeled motor vehicles, so they are examples of vehicles.

clue.text: Capital old lover

explanation.surface: An old flame from the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo, from Shakespeare's play, is used generally for an ardent male lover or womaniser.

clue.text: Broadcast account written up about fund-raising event in restaurant

indicators.note: about means the reversed letters go round the event
in a down clue, written up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account
a fete is an outdoor fund-raising fair

explanation.surface: A broadcast report describes a charity fair held in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: A fete is a British outdoor fair, often raising money for a church or school.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant, so it is a type of restaurant.

clue.text: Nothing good about monster

explanation.surface: There's nothing good to say about a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, so a monster.

clue.text: Flyer fast losing energy south of field

indicators.note: losing means one letter is dropped from the word for fast

explanation.surface: A flier fast running out of energy lands south of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'south of' puts the reduced word below LEA. 'Flyer' suggests a bird or pilot; it is a handbill.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyer is a printed sheet handed out for advertising, which is a leaflet.

clue.text: Structure for play with unknown actors in club one organised

indicators.note: in means the first pieces sit inside the rearranged letters
organised means arranged into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast

explanation.surface: A theatre club puts on a play with unknown actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' and 'actors' suggest the theatre; the play is children's play.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncy castle is an inflatable structure children jump on, built for play.

clue.text: Cutting back, cutting total level

indicators.note: something cutting into a word splits it and sits inside it
going back means the word for the first cutting is read from its end

parts.note: a tart or cutting remark is sharp

explanation.surface: Reads like a report on budget cuts: scaling back, slashing the overall figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'cutting's do different jobs: the first is the word to reverse, the second says it goes into the total.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer or tier, of rock or of society, so it means a level.

clue.text: Change of rules, I'll bet, securing very wonderful solution

indicators.note: a change of the letters means they are put in another order
securing means holding, so the rearranged letters hold another inside

explanation.surface: A gambler bets that a rule change will be a brilliant fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A silver bullet is a simple, magical-seeming remedy for a hard problem, as for killing werewolves.

clue.text: Hotchpotch in newspaper in Portuguese city

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside the city name

parts.note: Faro is a city in the Algarve
rag is a dismissive word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A jumbled mess appears in a local paper in the Algarve.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused mixture, just as a hotchpotch is a muddled jumble of things.

clue.text: Plants survive beginnings of rough weather, bad sort

indicators.note: a bad arrangement is a wrong one, so the next word's letters are reordered

parts.note: to survive is to live on

indicators.note: beginnings asks for only the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Some hardy greenery holds out against a storm, though it is a poor kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverworts are small flowerless green plants related to mosses, growing in damp places.

clue.text: Valley in jungle neglected

indicators.note: the answer is found in the run of letters across the next two words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A valley lies forgotten deep in the jungle.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland or Ireland, so it means valley directly.

clue.text: Large fellow blundering into conflict one ignored at party?

indicators.note: something blundering moves clumsily, so the letters of the word before it stumble into a new order
into means these letters go inside the word for conflict

explanation.surface: A big man stumbles into a fight, while someone else stands unnoticed at the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallflower is a shy person left without a dance partner, standing by the wall at a party.

clue.text: Experience, not fine for fish

indicators.note: not means this letter is left out of the word for experience

parts.note: to experience something is to feel it
F is the pencil-grade and abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Someone experienced but not fine is fishing for something.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove F from FEEL to leave EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The eel is a long snakelike fish found in rivers and seas.

clue.text: Hint about art not treated critically

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are changed in order
about means the word for hint wraps around the other letters

explanation.surface: An art critic gestures at a piece that has not been assessed critically.
explanation.definitionFit: Critically can mean crucially or significantly, as does the adverb meaning most significantly.

clue.text: Oil painter initially silent, upset about job

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of the word before it
about means the reversed word wraps around the job
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top

explanation.surface: An oil painter, at first quiet, gets upset about their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil painter' runs together in the surface; 'Oil' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum is crude oil, the mineral oil extracted from underground.

clue.text: Do pioneering work in club containing lounge and bar

indicators.note: containing means the word for club holds the next word inside it

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a club with a lounge and a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge and bar' sounds like rooms in the club; they are verbs and nouns giving letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaze a trail is an idiom for being first to do something new, as early explorers marked a path.

clue.text: Sincere, not caring? Not he

indicators.note: not means these two letters are taken out of the word for uncaring

explanation.surface: Is he sincere or just uncaring? Apparently not him.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means without guile or pretence, so naturally sincere and genuine.

clue.text: Music quiz, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter moves to the end of the word for quiz

explanation.surface: A music quiz round, perhaps with contestants going from first to last.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican popular music style, forerunner of reggae, so it is a kind of music.

clue.text: Coast said to be rocky coming into view

indicators.note: rocky means unstable, so the letters of the word before it are shaken into a new order
coming into means the rearranged letters enter the word for view

explanation.surface: A rocky shoreline appears on the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like a description of the coast, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaside is the coast, especially as a place for holidays.

clue.text: Former line put away

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: An old railway line has been closed and stored away.
explanation.definitionFit: Late can mean recently dead or no longer in office, as in the late president, so former.

clue.text: Firm receiving tips from usual adviser

indicators.note: receiving means the word for firm takes other letters inside it
tips are the two ends of the following word

explanation.surface: A company takes advice from its regular adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as a company but is the adjective for steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant is a professional paid to give expert advice, so an adviser.

clue.text: Disposes of small rooms according to report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: cells are small rooms, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: An estate agent reports getting rid of some poky rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell goods is to dispose of them for money, so sells means disposes of.

clue.text: Chief ornamental carving

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the person in charge
second meaning: a carved knob on a ceiling or vault

explanation.walkthrough: In architecture a boss is the carved ornament where the ribs of a vaulted ceiling meet.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both the head of an organisation and a raised decorative carved knob.

clue.text: Unsightly building in Spain certainly rushed, short of time

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so this letter is dropped from the word for rushed

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: An ugly block in Spain was certainly put up in a hurry without enough time.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, typically a badly designed building or structure.

clue.text: Silo we rebuilt, about right, not towering

indicators.note: rebuilt means constructed again in a different form, so these letters are rearranged
about means the rearranged letters go round another letter

explanation.surface: Farmers rebuilding a grain silo keep it modest in height.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-rise building has few storeys, the opposite of a towering high-rise block.

clue.text: Series for children located around unchanging southern bay?

indicators.note: around means the word for located wraps the rest

parts.note: the bay is a laurel tree

explanation.surface: A children's series set around a sleepy, never-changing bay in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' suggests a stretch of coast; it is the laurel, a kind of tree, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame Street is the long-running American TV programme for young children with the Muppets.
